description: For the pool operator, when a producer reports sign or dial failures, or before and after a KES rotation. panels.title: Signing timing: where does a sign's time go, against the 500 ms timeout?
Signing Timing: Producer Round Trip, Agent Sign, Guard Write
panels.description: Time spent signing each block header, as the mean per sign over 15m windows, so one point is one sign (or the average of the signs in that window). The histogram buckets (0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5 s) are too coarse for quantiles at a few signs an hour. Producer round trip (orange): the producer's view, from sending the sign request to holding the signature, per producer alias. Agent sign (grey): KES signing inside the agent, per profile. Guard write (purple): the mean of every write the agent makes to a shared slot-guard store, per profile, including writes for refused headers, failed signs, key installs and evolutions; empty with a guard file. Agent sign already includes its guard write. Round trip minus agent sign is time outside the agent's measurement (network, TLS and the producer's client), and only approximately, since the two means cover different requests. Producer series ignore the Namespace, Profile and Replica variables: the producer metric carries no label linking it to an agent, so it covers every producer in the datasource. The shaded bands are the budget: amber from 250 ms, half the producer's 500 ms sign timeout, red from 400 ms, close enough to it that an ordinary slow moment loses a block (Dingo's KES agent client gives up on a sign after 500 ms by default, set by `CARDANO_SHELLEY_KES_AGENT_SIGN_TIMEOUT`, which Dingo allows under 1 s, and the block is then not forged). **Healthy: every point below the amber band.**

panels.title: Sign Budget: Mean Time Against the 500 ms Timeout
panels.description: Three dials for the mean time of a sign over the dashboard range, each drawn against the producer's 500 ms sign timeout (set by `CARDANO_SHELLEY_KES_AGENT_SIGN_TIMEOUT`, which Dingo allows under 1 s). **Producer round trip**: what the producer waits, request sent to signature held, for every producer in the datasource: the producer metric carries no label linking it to an agent, so this dial ignores the Namespace, Profile and Replica variables and is not comparable to a filtered agent dial. **Agent sign**: the whole sign inside the agent, including its guard write. **Guard write**: the mean of every write to a shared slot-guard store, including writes for refused headers, failed signs, key installs and evolutions. The dials average different sets of requests, so they do not nest exactly: the gap between the first and second dial is only an estimate of the time outside the agent (network, TLS and the producer's client). **Healthy: all three green, under 250 ms.** Amber from 250 ms, red from 400 ms: that close to the timeout an ordinary slow moment loses a block. If the guard-write dial is nearly as high as the agent-sign dial, the database is the whole cost. Empty when no sign was requested in the range.

panels.title: Sign and Guard Write by Replica
panels.description: The same two agent-side timings as the panel above, split by replica instead of by profile: the mean per sign over 15-minute windows of the whole sign (`bursa_kesagent_sign_duration_seconds`) and of every shared slot-guard store write (`bursa_kesagent_slot_guard_write_duration_seconds`), which includes writes outside the signs shown. A replica whose guard write is consistently higher is the one with the slower guard store. **Healthy: replicas close together and below the amber band** (amber from 250 ms, red from 400 ms, close to the 500 ms sign timeout). Points, because signs are sparse.

panels.title: Signs by Replica
panels.description: Which replica served the signs over the dashboard range. With PreferClose routing a producer uses the replica in its own zone while it is ready, so the split follows which producers had leader slots; a replica name that is no longer running is a pod that was replaced inside the range. **Healthy: signs on whichever replica is closest to each producer, none lost in a failover.** A replica that never appears although its zone's producer forged is not reachable from it. Empty when no sign was requested in the range.

panels.title: Signs by Profile and Result
panels.description: Signs over the dashboard range by profile (one profile per pool), with every failed sign in one red slice. Each block a pool forges is one header sign, so this is also each pool's share of the blocks signed through the agent. **Healthy: no red slice.** The total should match Agent signs on Forging Health. Empty when no sign was requested in the range.

panels.title: Slot guard: refusals and key evolutions
Slot-Guard Refusals and Store Errors
panels.description: Per hour, by profile: headers the slot guard refused, by reason - equivocation (a second body for an already signed slot) or rollback (an older slot or period) - and guard store calls that timed out or failed. **Healthy: every line at zero.** No line at all means no scrape in that hour, which says nothing about the guard. Equivocation means two active producers on one pool; rollback a producer on a stale fork; a store error fails the sign without being a refusal, so check the slot-guard store.

panels.title: Key Evolutions and Keys Served
panels.description: KES key forward-evolutions per hour, and KES keys pushed to producers (serve-key mode). **Expected: one evolution per KES period (1.5 days) per profile on each replica**; none for longer than that means the key is not advancing and signs will fail on period errors. With every producer in sign mode, **zero keys served is expected**; anything else means a profile is handing out key material.

panels.title: Profiles by replica
panels.description: One line per namespace, profile and replica: current and last signable KES period, periods left, opcert issue number, exhausted and guard-fresh flags, time since the last sign, and signs, errors, refusals and store errors over the dashboard range. **Healthy: all replicas of a profile agree on every key column**; a mismatch means one replica did not pick up a rotation. Only replicas reporting metrics at the end of the selected range are listed: a pod replaced inside the time range drops out, and its signs stay in the header total and in Signs by Replica.

panels.title: KES Key Fuel: Periods Left per Profile
panels.description: A fuel gauge per profile: KES periods left on the key the agent holds (last signable period minus the current period, the lowest across replicas), on a dial that is full at 62 periods, a fresh key. One period is 1.5 days. **Healthy: green, more than 8 periods.** Amber at 8 or fewer, where dingo-operator should be rotating the key; red under 4 (6 days), where the pool stops forging soon unless a new key is installed. The rotation itself is on **Operator**.

panels.title: Replica Readiness
panels.description: Readiness of each agent pod over time. **Healthy: solid green on both.** A red stretch on one replica is covered by the other; overlapping red stretches are a signing outage.
